title: Pointwise left Kan extension of coherent space-valued diagrams
statement:
Use the universes, quasicategories, coherent diagrams, functor categories and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the infinity category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ of $\mathcal W$-small spaces of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $A,B$ be $\mathcal W$-small quasicategories and $v:A\to B$ a coherent functor. Functor categories are formed in a further universe. For $b\in B$, let $(v\downarrow b)$ be the coherent comma category with objects $(a,\alpha:v(a)\to b)$, commuting triangles, and their higher simplices; explicitly it is
$$A\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B}\{b\}.$$
For a coherent $F:A\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ there exist a coherent $v_!F:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ and a transformation $\eta_F:F\to(v_!F)v$ such that, for every coherent $G:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$, the map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})}(v_!F,G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})}(F,Gv),\qquad \theta\longmapsto(\theta v)\eta_F$$
is an equivalence of spaces, natural in $G$. For every $b$, the cocone with components $F(a)\xrightarrow{\eta_{F,a}}(v_!F)(v(a))\xrightarrow{(v_!F)(\alpha)}(v_!F)(b)$ is colimiting on the diagram $(v\downarrow b)\to A\xrightarrow{F}\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$. These are coherent cocones on the entire comma category. In particular, if $F=\Delta_A*$ and $G=\Delta_B*$ for the one-point space $*$, the mate $e:v_!\Delta_A*\to\Delta_B*$ of the identity $\Delta_A*\to\Delta_A*$ has, at $b$, the map from this comma-indexed colimit of the constant one-point diagram induced by its identity cocone.

source.place: HTT (April 9, 2017), Definition 4.3.2.2, Lemma 4.3.2.13, Proposition 4.3.2.15, Definition 4.3.3.2 and Proposition 4.3.3.7; arbitrary-functor comma form of pointwise left Kan extension. Read online, not archived in literature/. No matching Stacks tag: the assertion is quasicategorical, not ordinary Kan extension.

proof.text: Construct a small correspondence explicitly, rather than applying a full-inclusion theorem directly to the possibly non-fully-faithful $v$. Define $C_n$ to consist of triples $(s,a,b)$, where $s:[n]\to[1]$ is monotone, $I_0=s^{-1}(0)$, $a:\Delta^{I_0}\to A$, and $b:\Delta^n\to B$ satisfy $b|_{\Delta^{I_0}}=va$. For $I_0=\varnothing$ the $a$ datum is unique. Operators restrict all these data. The all-zero and all-one subsets give full inclusions $i:A\hookrightarrow C$ and $j:B\hookrightarrow C$; they contain all vertices between them. This is exactly the underlying relative nerve in [lem-cbc-marked-relative-nerve-quillen], applied to the strict $[1]$-diagram $A^\natural\xrightarrow{v}B^\natural$. Indeed, in its subset formula all components with maximum labeled zero are restrictions of $a$, and all those with maximum labeled one are restrictions of $b$. The marking is legitimate because applying a simplicial functor to inverse-and-triangle witnesses preserves equivalences. By [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] these two marked objects are fibrant, hence the diagram is projectively fibrant. The relative-nerve theorem and [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] make $C\to\Delta^1$ a cocartesian fibration. In particular it is an inner fibration by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and filling the projected inner horn in $\Delta^1$ and then lifting proves that $C$ is a quasicategory. All its degrees are $\mathcal W$-small, since the displayed data are finite-simplex maps between $\mathcal W$-small simplicial sets.

source.place: Definition 3.2.5.2 and Proposition 3.2.5.21; explicit relative nerve for the interval diagram A to B (agent expansion).

proof.text: Define $r:C\to B$ by $r(s,a,b)=b$. Then $ri=v$ and $rj=1_B$. There is a specified transformation $\tau:1_C\to jr$: on an $n$-simplex $((s,a,b),t)$ of $C\times\Delta^1$, replace $s$ by $\max(s,t)$, restrict $a$ to its new zero block, and keep $b$. These operations commute with every simplicial operator. At the two interval endpoints this is respectively $(s,a,b)$ and $j(b)$. Moreover $\tau j$ and $r\tau$ are the identity transformations, because on the all-one block the formula changes nothing and $r$ forgets the block. Put $u=\tau i:i\to jv$; its component at $a$ is the mixed edge represented by $1_{v(a)}$. These are actual coherent transformations, including their simplices, not just arrows in a homotopy category.

source.place: Section 4.3.3, proof of Proposition 4.3.3.7, cylinder retraction and homotopy; explicit max formula for the chosen relative-nerve model (agent).

proof.text:
For $c\in C$ put $K_c=A\times_C C_{/c}$ using the join slice in [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Each is a small quasicategory: pulling back a right fibration preserves its horn lifting property by filling the same square before pullback, and an inner horn then fills over the quasicategory $A$. The explicit simplex formula gives $K_{i(a)}=A_{/a}$ and
$$K_{j(b)}=A\times_B B_{/b}.$$
For the latter equality a simplex in $C_{/j(b)}$ with initial face in $A$ has zero-labeled initial vertices and a final one-labeled vertex; its remaining data are exactly $a:\Delta^n\to A$ and $\beta:\Delta^{n+1}\to B$ ending at $b$ with initial face $va$. To compare with the coherent arrow comma $J_b=(v\downarrow b)$, use [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence]: its comparison $B_{/b}\to T_b=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_B\{b\}$ lies over $B$. Both projections are right fibrations by the slice theorem and [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration]. Its maps on vertex fibers are equivalences by [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers]. Under the right-fibration classification [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] it therefore gives a pointwise equivalence of presheaves, hence a coherent equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Pull back this equivalence of classified right fibrations along $v$; the inverse and its two homotopies pull back as well. This proves that the actual comparison $d_b:K_{j(b)}\to J_b$ is an equivalence over $A$. Its formula is the restriction of each join simplex along $\rho_n:[n]\times[1]\to[n+1]$, so it also gives precisely the canonical coherent arrow cocone used in the item.

source.place: Sections 4.3.2–4.3.3 (local source slices); arrow-to-join comparison as in the cited slice and right-fibration nodes, with pullback justified by classification (agent).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-spaces-small-colimits-universe] with its small universe equal to $\mathcal W$ and an auxiliary larger universe. Every $K_c\to A\xrightarrow{F}\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ has a colimit, including an empty $K_c$. Use the right-cone version of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus]: apply its left-cone assertion to $K_c^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}^{\mathrm{op}}$, then reverse both diagrams and transformations. Clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] identifies $(K_c^{\mathrm{op}})^{\triangleleft}$ after reversal with $K_c^{\triangleright}$ and reverses the mapping spaces. The comparison on the fiber with fixed boundary supplies an actual join diagram with boundary $Fa_c$; its cocone is equivalent to the given colimit cocone. Its mapping formula, together with the cocone universal-property criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], express this as a colimit join diagram, equivalently a relative colimit for $p:\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}\to *$. By [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], the mapping square for a relative colimit has point-valued bottom row; its upper restriction map is an equivalence precisely by that join-cone mapping formula, since the cocone represents all cocones with fixed target vertex. The functor $p$ is an isofibration: inner horns fill in the quasicategory $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ and the identity equivalence of the point lifts to an identity. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-relative-kan-existence], for the full inclusion $i:A\subseteq C$ and the unique $C\to *$, produces $H:C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ with $Hi=F$ exactly, such that applying $H$ to every canonical cocone on $K_c$ gives a colimit. Its local colimits require only $\mathcal W$-small indexing shapes; the larger size of the category of spaces does not enlarge those shapes.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.2.13 and Proposition 4.3.2.15; the space colimits used in their hypotheses are those of the existing small-colimit node.

proof.text:
Set $L=Hj$ and $\eta=Hu:F=Hi\to Hjv=Lv$. At $b$ the local colimit supplied in step 4 has apex $Hj(b)=L(b)$ and index $K_{j(b)}$. Its component on $(a,\alpha:v(a)\to b)$ is $H$ of the corresponding mixed edge. Naturality of the explicit $\tau$ of step 2 identifies this edge after applying $H$ with
$$F(a)\xrightarrow{\eta_a}L(v(a))\xrightarrow{L(\alpha)}L(b),$$
because $\tau$ at $j(b)$ is the identity. This identity holds on the whole slice: apply that same naturality square to its simplices, not only its vertices. Convert its join cocone to the coherent transformation cocone by the right-cone comparison derived in step 4 from [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus]. The map $d_b$ of step 3 compares exactly that cocone with the displayed cocone on $J_b$. Naturality of $\tau$ gives an equivalence of these cocones with fixed apex; clause (1) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] preserves the colimit under this equivalence. By the index-equivalence clause (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence], applied to $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}\to *$, the latter is colimiting. This proves the requested pointwise clause with its entire coherent cocone, not merely an equivalence of its apex with some colimit object.

source.place: Definition 4.3.2.2 and Section 4.3.3; identification of the local cocone for the explicit interval correspondence (agent).

proof.text:
For any $G:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$, restriction along $j$ gives
$$R_j:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})}(H,Gr)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})}(L,G).$$
An inverse is $S_j(\theta)=(\theta r)(H\tau)$. Indeed $R_jS_j(\theta)=\theta$, since $rj=1$ and $\tau j=1$. For $\phi:H\to Gr$, naturality along $\tau$ gives $(\phi jr)(H\tau)\simeq ((Gr)\tau)\phi=\phi$, since $r\tau=1$. Applying this same naturality square with any simplicial parameter gives the homotopy of maps of full mapping spaces, so $S_jR_j\simeq1$. The mapping spaces here are Kan by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The composites with $H\tau$, with $\phi jr$ and their homotopies are formed coherently on whole mapping spaces of the quasicategory $\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})$ by the trivial Kan fibration of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine], which supplies composition, its associativity and unit homotopies; whiskering by $r$, $j$ and $\tau$ is strict precomposition. These formulas commute with coherent postcomposition in $G$, so $R_j$ is an equivalence natural in $G$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.3.3.7, retraction adjunction; the inverse and its homotopies are written explicitly here (agent).

proof.text:
The functor $H$ satisfies the source-colimit hypothesis at every $c\in C$ of [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction], by step 4. Apply that node to the two functors $H,Gr$ and the full inclusion $i$. It gives the equivalence
$$R_i:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})}(H,Gr)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})}(F,Gv).$$
Composing with $S_j$ of step 6 gives an equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}(L,G)$ to $\operatorname{Map}(F,Gv)$. Its actual formula is
$$R_iS_j(\theta)=((\theta r)(H\tau))i=(\theta v)\eta.$$
Naturality in $G$ is that of restriction and of the explicit inverse in step 6, including coherent transformations and their higher parameters. With $v_!F=L$, this is the mapping-space equivalence specified by the item. No fullness assumption on $v$ has been introduced.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.2.12 and Proposition 4.3.3.7, mapping-space universal property after the full-inclusion reduction.

proof.text:
Specialize to $F=\Delta_A*$ and $G=\Delta_B*$. Let $e:L\to\Delta_B*$ be the mate of $1_{\Delta_A*}$ under step 7, with its specified coherent identification $(ev)\eta\simeq1$. Postcompose the entire pointwise colimit cocone of step 5 with $e_b$. Naturality of $e$ identifies its component on $(a,\alpha)$ with
$$e_bL(\alpha)\eta_a\simeq (\Delta_B*)(\alpha)e_{v(a)}\eta_a\simeq1_*.$$
The first homotopy is the naturality square, and the second is the mate equation; both are coherent on all comma simplices, the composites and their associativity homotopies being those of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. Thus this is the identity cocone of the constant one-point diagram. The universal property of the already established colimit identifies $e_b$ with the map induced by that cocone, proving the last clause. This also covers an empty comma category: its colimit is the initial space and its induced map to $*$ is the empty-cocone map.

source.place: Section 4.3.3, adjunction mate; specialization and normalization of its pointwise cocone (agent).

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 2, foundational coherent derived-coefficient adjunction; explicit relative-nerve reduction following online HTT 3.2.5 and 4.3.2–4.3.3 and the cited DAG interfaces. HTT archival copy requested in report.
